$comment: ELF64 EXECUTABLE (ET_EXEC) for x86_64 Linux. Second ELF schema (plan 14 LK1 cycle 2, 2026-05-30). Consumed by `src/link/format/elf.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. Differs from `elf64-x86_64-linux.format.json` (the .o schema) in: `elf.type = exec`, sections carry `virtualAddress` (used as sh_addr), top-level `entryPoint` names the entry symbol (resolved against AssembledModule at link time). Cycle-2 scope: self-contained modules (zero relocations). Modules with relocations fail loud — the cross-reference applier lives at LK6 (D-LK4-5 + D-LK4-6 + D-LK1-3).
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: ELF has NO image field for a stack SIZE on ANY flavor -- PT_GNU_STACK encodes stack EXECUTABILITY, not size. The kernel sizes the initial thread's stack from the process limit (`ulimit -s` / setrlimit RLIMIT_STACK) and further threads from pthread_attr_setstacksize, so nothing the linker writes can change it. A `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request is therefore REFUSED with that remedy rather than silently dropped -- which is also why the sqlite full tier passes on Linux (8 MiB by default) and overflowed on Windows at 1 MiB.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c-subset long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Linux/POSIX header names are matched BYTE-EXACT -- `#include <Stdio.h>` does NOT name `stdio.h`, and a conforming toolchain must reject it. REQUIRED closed-enum field: the loader rejects a missing or unknown value. DSS performs the comparison ITSELF (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) rather than calling fs::exists and inheriting the BUILD HOST's convention -- without that, an elf target built on Windows/macOS silently ACCEPTED `<Stdio.h>` and emitted a real object (MEASURED 2026-08-04).
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: System V / ELF applies NO decoration to a C identifier -- the linker-visible name IS the identifier. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`nm -D /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6`, WSL Ubuntu): glibc exports `exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5`, `printf@@GLIBC_2.2.5` and `fstat64@@GLIBC_2.33` under exactly their C spellings. THE SAME COMMAND IS ALSO WHY `none` IS A POSITIVE ANSWER AND NOT AN ABSENCE: `_exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5` is exported TOO and is a DIFFERENT FUNCTION -- POSIX `_exit(2)`, which does NOT flush stdio -- so a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would not merely produce an ugly name, it would silently bind every `exit` to the non-flushing wrapper and lose buffered output. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c-subset/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: SysV/GNU LSB-first bit-field packing (byte-ABI-exact to gcc). OS/format-determined (x86_64 serves both ELF and PE), so on the format not the target. See elf64-x86_64-linux for the full rule.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: SysV x86_64 `long double` is the x87 80-bit extended format stored 16/16. The axis resolves the c-subset row to F80 — declarations/layout/sizeof work; VALUE arithmetic walls loud (L_UnsupportedLoweringForOpcode) until D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH lands. OS/format-determined (the same x86_64 target serves pe64's f64), so the axis lives here next to dataModel.
$entryPointComment: Empty entryPoint defaults the walker to module.functions[0] (cycle-2 convention). Once D-LK1-1 closes (real symbol-name thread through HIR→LIR→AssembledFunction), this field will name the entry symbol (e.g. '_start' for Linux/glibc, 'main' for hand-rolled execs) and the walker will resolve it by name. When D-LK10-ENTRY Slice C lands, the linker prepends a synthetic `_start` trampoline as module.functions[0] and the schema's entryPoint names the USER fn (the trampoline's call target).
$externCallDispatchComment: ELF resolves imports through the PLT: the linker synthesizes a PLT stub per extern (jmp through the GOT slot) and points the extern symbol's VA at the STUB, so the call site is a PLAIN DIRECT call (E8 disp32 = call rel32 to the stub). An indirect-slot (FF 15) call site would dereference the stub's CODE bytes as a pointer -> SIGSEGV. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH.
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED + D-LK-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-UNCONSULTED-BY-ELF-AND-MACHO-WRITERS: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the linker keeps one. ELF puts the weakness in the SYMBOL's own BINDING field: STB_WEAK (2) in the high nibble of Elf64_Sym.st_info, gABI 4.18. No section flag and no separate per-symbol flag bit is involved, which is exactly what distinguishes `symbol-binding` from COFF's `comdat` (a per-SECTION duplicate-resolution policy) and from Mach-O's `symbol-flag` (N_WEAK_DEF set ALONGSIDE an ordinary binding). Written by `stbForBinding` in src/link/format/elf.cpp. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. `elf::encode` READS this key -- ONCE, covering every ELF flavor, because the alias pass reaches stbForBinding on ET_REL, ET_EXEC and ET_DYN alike -- and refuses loud on a dialect it has no encoder for, so the declaration cannot drift away from what is actually emitted. The loader additionally refuses this key at LOAD when the declared dialect is not one the resolved backend's walker writes (ObjectFormatBackend::weakDefinitionDialects), so a mis-declaration fails at its source rather than at the first weak definition.
$dataImportBindingComment: D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT: extern library DATA objects (libc stdout/stderr/stdin, POSIX `__environ`) bind GOT-INDIRECT — the walker reserves a GOT slot per imported object AFTER the function slots and emits one R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT (6) against it in .rela.dyn; ld.so writes the LIBRARY OBJECT's address into the slot at load and the shared c117/c149 GotIndirect lowering (lea-of-slot + deref) reads it. IDENTICAL to the pie/dyn siblings' declaration, and that sameness is the point: this walker now OBEYS this key instead of re-deriving the model from the image flavour. ★★ WHY THIS IS NOT COPY-RELOCATION ANY MORE, AND WHY THAT MECHANISM NO LONGER EXISTS AT ALL (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET): this format used to declare "copy-relocation" — reserve a .bss slot of the object's exact size, export the symbol as a DEFINED OBJECT there, emit one R_X86_64_COPY (5), and let ld-linux memcpy the library's object in so every image referencing THAT NAME converged on the exec's copy. ✔MEASURED, that convergence is NAME-SCOPED and therefore UNSOUND for any object with ALIASES: glibc x86_64 exports ONE object at 0x20ad58 under THREE names (`__environ` GLOBAL, `_environ` and `environ` WEAK), so an exec claiming only `__environ` had `__libc_start_main` write envp into ITS copy while libc's own `environ` slot was NEVER written — a third-party libtcl8.6.so reading `environ` got NULL and SIGSEGV'd in TclSetupEnv, with no diagnostic from anything. C23 6.2.2 says an identifier with external linkage denotes the SAME object throughout the program; copy-relocation split one object in two. The enum value is DELETED, not merely unused (an accepted-but-undeclared value is one JSON edit away from the whole class), so spelling it here is now REFUSED AT LOAD naming this file. ★ GOT-INDIRECT IS LEGAL IN THIS NON-PIE ET_EXEC — do not "fix" it back: a non-PIE exec has a .got like any image and R_*_GLOB_DAT rows in .rela.dyn are processed by ld.so at load with no PIE requirement (✔MEASURED: this format's own binaries run). Copy relocation existed only to hand non-PIC code a link-time-CONSTANT address for an object the image does not define; got-indirect needs no such constant. A format WITHOUT this field rejects data imports loud at the linker's pre-walker gate (a data symbol bound through the function-import machinery would read jump-stub bytes as the object's value).
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-LK1-ELF-EXEC-DATA-SECTIONS (rodata) + D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER (writable `.data` + zero-fill `.bss`) + D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (thread-local `.tdata`/`.tbss`, TLS C1): the ELF ET_EXEC walker emits `.rodata` (read-only, R+X PT_LOAD), `.data` (mutable initialized globals, R+W PT_LOAD), `.bss` (zero-init globals, R+W PT_LOAD, NOBITS), `.tdata` (initialized thread-local template, opens the R+W PT_LOAD, covered by PT_TLS), and `.tbss` (zero-fill thread-local extent, NOBITS, PT_TLS memsz only — NO file/segment footprint) from `AssembledModule.dataItems` per the item's `section`. The linker's pre-walker gate (linker.cpp) consults this set per-item. Cross-format agnosticism: this is the SAME field PE/Mach-O exec formats declare; the gate has zero format-name branches. tdata/tbss here is THE x86_64-linux opt-in — arm64-linux opts in at TLS C2, pe64 at C3, Mach-O at C4; until then their walkers ALSO carry a K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport belt.
$relroExecComment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (c145): `relro` (a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations — a const function-pointer table / `int *const p=&x;`) is advertised so the linker's pre-walker gate admits it. In the EXECUTABLE image the walker FOLDS a relro item into the writable `.data` section (the exec decision — 'treat relro like .data'; the loader writes the resolved target VA into the slot, and the read-only-after-relocation hardening of a separate GNU_RELRO segment is a nicety not required for correctness), so NO separate `.data.rel.ro` section row is declared here. The distinct `.data.rel.ro` + `.rela.data.rel.ro` (gcc's contract) is emitted only by the RELOCATABLE `.o` schema (elf64-x86_64-linux).
$tlsAccessComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): how code reaches a thread-local object's per-thread copy on this leg. local-exec = the ELF static-TLS model for a non-PIE executable: glibc's ld.so processes PT_TLS for every thread (the CSU runs before main on this ALWAYS-dynamic arm), sets fs.base, and stores the thread pointer's own address at fs:[0] (the tcbhead self-pointer) — so `mov r, fs:[0]` (segmentPrefixByte 100 = 0x64 fs-override, baseDisplacement 0) reads tp, and a symbol's address is tp + tpoff(sym) with tpoff a LINK-TIME constant (the tls-tpoff32 reloc; x86_64 Variant II ⇒ negative). MIR→LIR reads this block to emit the tlsbase + lea pair; a format WITHOUT the block fails loud K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport on the first thread-local access (pe64/macho omit it until their TLS cycles). PE later declares the SAME x86 primitive with config-only differences: model pe-indexed, 101 = 0x65 gs, baseDisplacement 0x58 (the TEB ThreadLocalStoragePointer).
$artifactProfilesComment: Profiles this format SERVES (plan 06 AP3) — a runnable console executable ⇒ cli. The format-side twin of the language's artifactProfiles[] (AP1): the driver fails loud (D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch) if a project's profile isn't in this set. A future shared-library format would declare ["lib"] with ZERO gate-code change — the gate is a generic set-membership, never a format-name branch.
$runtimeLibrariesComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the ROLE -> IMAGE table, and the SINGLE OWNER of 'which image plays which runtime role' for this format. The spine blocks below name a ROLE and the loader resolves it here; each block's resolved path is a DERIVED copy and ObjectFormatData::validate() re-checks the pair, so the two cannot drift. The table is not a pe concern that ELF merely inherits -- ELF is where the SPLIT IS ALREADY REAL, and that is the measured argument for a table over a single per-format CRT string: MEASURED 2026-08-10 (`nm -D`), the unwinder personality lives in libgcc_s.so.1 and libc.so.6 exports NO `_Unwind_*` symbol at all. Do NOT be fooled by `personality@@GLIBC_2.2.5` in libc -- that is the personality(2) SYSCALL wrapper, unrelated to unwinding. So on this format one image demonstrably cannot serve both cLibrary and unwindPersonality, whereas on pe64 they happen to coincide (ucrtbase exports `__C_specific_handler` at ord 30) -- a table PERMITS that sameness without ASSERTING it. This file declares only cLibrary today because it names only cLibrary: an unwindPersonality row would be INERT until ELF unwind lands and a `sehPersonality`-equivalent block names it, and validate() REFUSES an unnamed row rather than letting a stale image sit here unread. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this row and processExit refuses the format AT LOAD, naming this file.
$entryVerbsComment: UCRT-P4 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE): the program-entry materialization VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE -- what it is able to hand a program entry before calling it. * THE ACCEPTED ENTRY SET IS AN INTERSECTION, AND THIS FILE OWNS ONLY HALF OF IT. This key used to be `entryShapes` -- full { returns, params, materialization } rows -- which made the accepted SIGNATURES a format fact. They are not one: `int wmain(int, wchar_t**)` is a C spelling, and a linker format has no opinion on how a source language spells an entry, only on what it can hand one. So the signatures moved to their single owner, the language file's `entryFunctions` mapping (src/dss-config/sources/c-subset.lang.json), which declares each name->signature->verb; this key declares the VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE. A defined function is a program-entry candidate iff its name matches a declared language row, its signature matches that row, and that row's verb appears HERE. C23 3.4.1 requires an implementation to DOCUMENT its implementation-defined choices, so the documentation artifact is the PAIR of comments -- this one and $entryFunctionsComment -- each naming the other. Reading either alone tells you less than the truth. * WHY `argc-wargv` IS ABSENT, AND WHAT THAT NOW ACHIEVES: nothing on this platform produces a wide argument vector, so this format cannot realize the verb. That absence is the entire mechanism by which `wmain` is not a program entry here -- the language still declares `wmain -> argc-wargv`, the verb is not in this set, so the row does not survive the intersection and `wmain` is an ordinary function. MEASURED 2026-08-10 on HEAD 3e86a187 (build-dbg), BEFORE this: `int wmain(int, unsigned short**)` with no `main`, built for this format, was SELECTED AS THE LINUX ENTRY by a name-only scan and then refused by a message that asserted `wmain` WAS the Linux entry and prescribed adding a row to this very file to make it one. gcc's answer to that source is `undefined reference to 'main'`. A `main` + `wmain` program now BUILDS here and takes `main`, because exactly one candidate survives. * WHY THERE IS NO envp VERB YET, and why that is a cycle rather than a data addition: on ELF envp CANNOT be a third static offset -- processArgs above declares STATIC argcStackOffset/argvStackOffset, whereas envp sits at argv_base + (argc+1)*8, i.e. RUNTIME-COMPUTED. A new verb needs its own emitter and its own RUN witness (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE). * `none` is the verb `int main(void)` needs -- C23's () == (void) equivalence makes `int main()` resolve to it -- and declaring it is an ANSWER, not an omission: a no-argument entry needs no setup at all. * RED-ON-DISABLE: drop "argc-argv" from this list and every example whose entry is `main(int, char**)` becomes unresolvable on this format -- the language's argc-argv row no longer survives the intersection, so the program has no entry candidate at all and the build is REFUSED naming this key. Empty the list entirely and the format is refused AT LOAD (exec-flavored <-> non-empty entryVerbs is pinned in both directions), because the engine reads this emptiness as "this format starts no program".
$processExitComment: STDIO-FLUSH-AT-EXIT (2026-06-09): terminate via libc `exit(3)`, NOT the raw `exit_group(2)` syscall. The C standard says returning from `main` ≡ calling `exit(3)`, which flushes line-/full-buffered stdio + runs `atexit` handlers before the process dies. The prior raw `exit_group` syscall skipped that flush, so a program that did `puts("hello")` then returned exited cleanly but with stdout still buffered (empty on a pipe). By-name-import of libc `exit` makes the trampoline emit a DIRECT `call` to the PLT stub for `exit` (per externCallDispatch=direct-plt), exactly as a user-level FFI call (`puts`) lowers — so `exit` flushes stdout, runs atexit, then calls `_exit`/`exit_group` itself. This routes EVERY ELF program through the dynamic writer (libc.so.6 becomes a DT_NEEDED, a PLT stub + GOT slot is synthesized for `exit`, ld-linux resolves it) — the SAME machinery `extern_call_elf` already uses; a program whose ONLY extern is this `exit` works because it is identical in shape to the FFI case. importMangledName is the canonical C name `exit` (ELF adds no leading underscore -- this file's `cSymbolDecoration` declares scheme `none`, which since TF-C122 is where that answer lives; it used to be a C++ table keyed on the format kind). Uniform with macho (libSystem `exit`) + pe (kernel32 `ExitProcess`, which flushes via msvcrt's DLL-detach handler): all three terminate through a libc-level, stdio-flushing primitive.
$entryCallingConventionComment: SysV AMD64 calling convention — status (user fn return value in rax) is moved into argGprs[0] = rdi before SYSCALL. Read via `target.callingConventionByName("sysv_amd64")` at trampoline-build time.
$processArgsComment: c88 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ARGC-ARGV): program-entry argc/argv materialization. SysV AMD64 psABI §3.4.1 — at the process entry point the kernel/loader leaves argc (a machine word) at [rsp+0] and the NULL-terminated argv pointer vector IN PLACE starting at [rsp+8] (envp follows argv's NULL; not materialized — the c-subset entry signature is (int, char**)). The trampoline emits `mov rdi, [rsp+0]` (argc → argGprs[0]) + `lea rsi, [rsp+8]` (the vector's ADDRESS → argGprs[1]) BEFORE any SP adjustment and before `call main`. A main(void) simply ignores the two registers (C-legal) — signature-independent setup. Without this block, main(argc,argv) reads process-entry register garbage (the c87 sqlite3 shell crash: argc=846361312). Destination registers come from entryCallingConvention.argGprs[0..1] — never declared here (single source of truth).

elf.$comment: Elf64_Ehdr identity for an executable. type = ET_EXEC (2). class = ELFCLASS64; data = ELFDATA2LSB; osabi = sysv; machine = EM_X86_64 (62). pageAlign = 4096 (Linux x86_64 4 KB pages — kernel's PT_LOAD congruence requires p_vaddr % p_align == p_offset % p_align). ARM64 Linux on Apple Silicon / 64K configurations declares 16384 / 65536 in its own schema (D-LK6-3).
elf.$bindNowComment: Eager binding — the v1 stance per plan 14 §5 risk row. Emits DT_FLAGS_1 = DF_1_NOW so dyld resolves every GOT slot at load via R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT in .rela.dyn. Lazy upgrade (.rela.plt + R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT + 16-byte PLT0 resolver-trampoline) anchored at D-LK6-11; until then, the walker fails loud on bindNow=false.

sections.$comment: Executable code section. virtualAddress = 0x401000 — conventional Linux x86_64 base (0x400000) + 0x1000 to leave the first page for the Ehdr and program header table loaded alongside `.text` in the same PT_LOAD. This is a convention, not a kernel hard requirement: any page-aligned VA works as long as `p_vaddr % p_align == p_offset % p_align`. sh_addr is set to this; e_entry derives from this + entry-function offset. sh_flags = SHF_ALLOC | SHF_EXECINSTR (6); sh_addralign = 16 (x86_64 psABI).
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: Read-only initialized data (string literals, const/primitive globals). sh_type=SHT_PROGBITS(1); sh_flags=SHF_ALLOC(2) — readable, NOT writable/executable (it is folded into the R+X text PT_LOAD this cycle, which is strictly less permissive than writable; W^X preserved). sh_addralign=8. virtualAddress=0 — the writer COMPUTES the rodata VA contiguously after .text (secText.virtualAddress + alignUp(text.size, 8)); a fixed VA would collide with .text. D-LK1-ELF-EXEC-DATA-SECTIONS.
sections.name: .rodata

sections.$comment: Writable initialized data (mutable primitive/aggregate globals). sh_type=SHT_PROGBITS(1); sh_flags=SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE(3) — readable + WRITABLE (a store into it must not fault). Placed in a SEPARATE R+W PT_LOAD from the R+X text/rodata so mutable data never shares a page with code (W^X). sh_addralign=8. virtualAddress=0 — the writer COMPUTES the `.data` VA (page-aligned writable segment after the read-only sections). D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER.
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: Zero-initialized data (tentative globals `int g;`). sh_type=SHT_NOBITS(8) — occupies NO file bytes; the loader zero-fills sh_size bytes at the section VA. sh_flags=SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE(3) — readable + writable. Contributes to the R+W PT_LOAD's p_memsz but NOT its p_filesz. sh_addralign=8. virtualAddress=0 — the writer COMPUTES the `.bss` VA (last in the writable segment). D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER.
sections.name: .bss

sections.$comment: Initialized THREAD-LOCAL template data (`thread_local int g = 7;` — D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, TLS C1). sh_type=SHT_PROGBITS(1); sh_flags=SHF_WRITE|SHF_ALLOC|SHF_TLS(0x403=1027) — the TLS bit is what tells inspectors (readelf/lldb) these bytes are a per-thread TEMPLATE, not process data. The walker places it as the FIRST file-backed member of the R+W PT_LOAD #2 and points PT_TLS at it (p_offset/p_vaddr=here, p_filesz=this section, p_memsz=+tbss); glibc's ld.so copies the template into every thread's static TLS block (main thread included — the CSU runs before main on the always-dynamic ELF arm). sh_addralign floor 1 — MEMBER-DRIVEN (the walker raises to the strictest member alignment, which also becomes PT_TLS p_align). Deliberately NOT the .data-style floor 8: PT_TLS p_align feeds the tpoff formulas (tpoff = offset - alignUp(memsz, p_align) on Variant II) and glibc's per-thread block placement, so a gratuitous floor would inflate every thread's block + diverge from the gcc-witnessed offsets (gcc: thread_local int -> sh_addralign 4, p_align 4). virtualAddress=0 — computed.
sections.name: .tdata

sections.$comment: Zero-fill THREAD-LOCAL template extent (`thread_local int g;` — D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, TLS C1). sh_type=SHT_NOBITS(8); sh_flags=SHF_WRITE|SHF_ALLOC|SHF_TLS(0x403=1027). Unlike `.bss` it occupies NO file bytes AND NO PT_LOAD memory — its span lives ONLY in PT_TLS p_memsz (the loader allocates + zeroes it per thread); sh_addr/sh_offset are the nominal just-past-.tdata values (the gcc overlap convention for NOBITS TLS). sh_addralign floor 1 — member-driven, same rationale as .tdata. virtualAddress=0 — computed.
sections.name: .tbss

sections.$comment: Symbol table — even in ET_EXEC files, .symtab is conventional for debugger support. sh_type = SHT_SYMTAB (2); sh_addralign = 8; sh_entsize = 24 (Elf64_Sym).
sections.name: .symtab

sections.$comment: Symbol-name string table. sh_type = SHT_STRTAB (3); addrAlign = 1.
sections.name: .strtab

sections.$comment: Section-header string table. sh_type = SHT_STRTAB (3); addrAlign = 1.
sections.name: .shstrtab

relocations.$comment: Relocation kinds are declared so the linker engine's cross-reference unifier (plan 13 §2.6) accepts any relocation tag the assembler stamps. In ET_EXEC cycle 2, the walker rejects modules whose AssembledFunctions carry ANY relocation entries (cycle scope: self-contained only). Resolved at LK6 D-LK4-5/D-LK4-6 + plan 14 D-LK1-3.
relocations.name: R_X86_64_PC32

relocations.$comment: D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (TLS C1): the local-exec thread-pointer-offset fixup — the disp32 of `lea r, [tp + tpoff32(sym)]`. kind=4 matches the target schema's `tls-tpoff32` row (Linear, width 4, absolute, tls:true); the walker patches the 4 bytes from its tpoff-valued symbolVa entry, so the exec image carries NO runtime reloc for it (link-time constant). nativeId = R_X86_64_TPOFF32 (23) — only meaningful for a future ET_REL emission of this kind, but the row's existence is what satisfies the linker's pre-walker cross-reference unifier + the walker's in-arm kind check.
relocations.name: R_X86_64_TPOFF32
